_about: Gaps and problems found while pulling data.

gaps.text: "Luke 10:30" (listed under parabole): STEPBible doesn't tag G3850 there. It's a related word at most; the note should say so or the reference should go.
"Romans 16:25" (listed under mysterion): STEPBible doesn't tag G3466 there. It's a related word at most; the note should say so or the reference should go.
Authorship, dating, audience, historical setting, cultural notes, map stops, the timeline, and chapter summaries come from no dataset. They're marked needs-review.
Range of meaning, English renderings, pronunciations, and notes are hand-written and need review. The STEPBible lexicon entry is shown alongside them.
Theographic's descriptions are Easton's Bible Dictionary (1897) and its dates are debated; neither is displayed.
The HelloAO Free Use Bible API and openbible.info aren't reachable from the build environment, so the WEB text and the cross-reference file come from GitHub mirrors (see the Sources page).
The Mediterranean, the Dead Sea, and Samaria aren't central to Matthew's story; they're pulled to draw the map. Egypt is off the map.
Theographic has no records for the magi, the devil, or groups like the Pharisees and Sadducees. Those stay hand-written.
Chapters 14 to 28 have text, people, places, and cross-references from the data, but no hand-written context notes yet.
Emmanouel appears only once in the New Testament; its other uses (Isaiah 7:14, 8:8) are in the Hebrew Bible, which the Greek tagging doesn't cover.
Manuscripts differ at 8:28 (Gadarenes, Gerasenes, or Gergesenes), so where the pigs scene happened is debated; we show Gadara as OpenBible locates it.
